labels.key: How to read the status marks
labels.examples_intro: Each row is a family of examples and each column a part of the theory. A mark gives the strongest status reached for that part in that example; select it to read its scope. Each row below opens to its statements.
labels.grid: Status of each part of the theory in each family of examples
labels.grid_caption: Rows are families of examples; columns are parts of the theory; each mark gives a status.
labels.grid_hint: Select a mark for its scope, or a family of examples for its statements. In the table, the arrow keys move between marks.
labels.terms_intro: Definitions of the specialised terms used above. In the text, a term with a dotted underline opens its definition.
labels.key_cells: In the table of examples, further marks:
labels.contents_examples: {rows} families of examples, {cols} parts of the theory

cell_glosses.checked: Proved and independently checked for this example, within the scope given.
cell_glosses.partial: Established only for a restricted model, a neighbouring statement or a negative result; the part itself is not established.
cell_glosses.pending: A proposed construction has a written argument, with the stated unresolved proof obligations.
cell_glosses.published: Known in the literature for this example.
cell_glosses.not posed: No precise statement has yet been formulated for this example.
cell_glosses.refuted form: The statement in the form first posed is false; the scope gives the true replacement where one is known.
